pattern.name: microservices_boundary_definition
pattern.description: Define clear boundaries between microservices based on business capabilities
pattern.when_to_use: When decomposing monolith or designing new microservices

implementation_steps.step: Identify business capabilities and bounded contexts
Define service boundaries based on domain-driven design

example.code:
# Service boundaries based on business capabilities services: - name: user-service responsibilities: [user_management, authentication, authorization] data_ownership: [users, profiles, permissions]
- name: order-service responsibilities: [order_processing, order_validation, order_history] data_ownership: [orders, order_items]
- name: inventory-service responsibilities: [stock_management, product_catalog, pricing] data_ownership: [products, inventory, prices]
- name: payment-service responsibilities: [payment_processing, refunds, billing] data_ownership: [payments, transactions, invoices]

pattern.name: event_driven_communication
pattern.description: Implement asynchronous communication using events to decouple services
pattern.when_to_use: When services need to communicate without tight coupling

implementation_steps.step: Define event schemas and naming conventions
Implement error handling and dead letter queues

pattern.name: cqrs_implementation
pattern.description: Separate command and query responsibilities for optimized performance
pattern.when_to_use: When read and write patterns differ significantly

implementation_steps.step: Design separate models for commands and queries

pattern.name: api_gateway_pattern
pattern.description: Centralize API management and cross-cutting concerns
pattern.when_to_use: When managing multiple microservices or complex API ecosystem

pattern.name: database_scaling_strategy
pattern.description: Design database architecture for horizontal scaling
pattern.when_to_use: When anticipating high data volume or traffic growth

implementation_steps.step: Analyze data access patterns and hot spots
Choose appropriate scaling strategy (sharding, replication, partitioning)
Implement connection pooling and load balancing
Set up monitoring and failover mechanisms

pattern.name: service_mesh_implementation
pattern.description: Implement service mesh for microservice communication and management

implementation_steps.step: Choose service mesh technology (Istio, Linkerd, Consul)

example.code: apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3 kind: VirtualService metadata: name: user-service spec: hosts: - user-service http: - match: - uri: prefix: "/api/users" route: - destination: host: user-service subset: v1 weight: 90 - destination: host: user-service subset: v2 weight: 10 fault: delay: percentage: value: 0.1 fixedDelay: 5s --- apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3 kind: DestinationRule metadata: name: user-service spec: host: user-service trafficPolicy: loadBalancer: simple: LEAST_CONN connectionPool: tcp: maxConnections: 100 http: http1MaxPendingRequests: 50 maxRequestsPerConnection: 10 circuitBreaker: consecutiveErrors: 3 interval: 30s baseEjectionTime: 30s

pattern.name: message_queue_pattern
pattern.description: Implement asynchronous message processing for decoupled communication
pattern.when_to_use: When services need reliable, asynchronous communication

implementation_steps.step: Choose message broker (RabbitMQ, Kafka, AWS SQS)
Set up monitoring and dead letter handling

pattern.name: oauth2_implementation
pattern.description: Implement OAuth2 for secure API authentication
pattern.when_to_use: When securing APIs that need user authentication

implementation_steps.step: Choose OAuth2 flow (Authorization Code, Client Credentials, etc.)

pattern.name: api_rate_limiting
pattern.description: Implement rate limiting to protect APIs from abuse
pattern.when_to_use: When exposing public APIs or managing resource usage

implementation_steps.step: Choose rate limiting algorithm (token bucket, sliding window)
Configure rate limits per user/IP/API key
Implement distributed rate limiting for scalability
Add proper headers and error responses

pattern.name: caching_strategy
pattern.description: Implement multi-layer caching for optimal performance
pattern.when_to_use: When dealing with high read loads or expensive computations

implementation_steps.step: Choose appropriate caching levels (memory, Redis, CDN)
Set up cache warming and preloading
Monitor cache hit rates and performance

example.scenario: Multi-layer caching with Redis and memory
